newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's new CPF scheme launched on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's new CPF scheme launched on Wednesday.

text.p: New rules for Singapore's Central Provident Fund (CPF) retirement investment scheme became effective on Wednesday, the CPF Board said.
The new rules, first announced by the CPF Board in March 1996, merge the Basic and Enhanced Investment Schemes to create the new CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS).

The new programme widens investment opportunities by fixing the minimum qualifying criteria to the former level of the basic scheme, but allowing the use of broader investment instruments than allowed under the old enhanced scheme.
These instruments include shares and loan stocks, unit trusts and managed funds, as well as Singapore government bonds, approved bank deposits and endowment insurance policies.
Up to 10 percent of funds can also be held in gold.
CPFIS will enable up to 80 percent of funds above a minimum of Singapore $45,000 to be invested in approved instruments.

The creation of CPFIS supplements the second stage of a three stage reform of CPF investment regulations, which effective from January 1 allows CPF funds to be invested in stocks in Malaysia, Thailand, South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong.

The first stage allowed investment in foreign stocks listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange from January 1 1995. The third stage, scheduled for January 1 1999, will permit investments in the U.S., Japan and Germany.
